items.title: NASA confirms Artemis II is go for April 1 moon launch

featured_image.name: When is Nasa's Moon mission launch and what will Artemis do? - BBC

items.description:
Four astronauts are one week away from becoming the first humans to travel to the moon in more than half a century. NASA is targeting April 1 for the launch of Artemis 2, a 10-day test flight that will send a crew around the far side of the moon and back aboard the Orion spacecraft atop the Space Launch System rocket.[1][2]

The crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialist Christina Koch from NASA, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — entered quarantine in Houston on March 18 and will fly to Kennedy Space Center roughly five days before launch. The mission will make Glover the first person of color, Koch the first woman, and Hansen the first non-American to travel to the moon.[3][4][2]

items.title: Trump sends 15-point peace plan to Iran as Hormuz opens to some ships

featured_image.name: Trump's team game planning for potential Iran peace talks

items.description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that he had sent a peace plan to Iran and expressed optimism about ending nearly a month of war, as Tehran informed the United Nations it would permit "non-hostile" vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz — a narrow waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global oil normally flows.[1][2]

items.title: Astronomers spot two planets forming around a young star like our sun

featured_image.name: Astronomers have spotted two giant gas plants forming around ...

items.description: An international team of astronomers has confirmed the discovery of a second planet forming in the dust disk surrounding the young star WISPIT 2, making it only the second known system where two planets have been directly observed taking shape around their host star. The findings, published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, offer what researchers describe as the closest analog yet to our own solar system in its infancy.[1][2]

items.title: Brazil court places Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds

featured_image.name: Brazil court places Bolsonaro under house arrest on health ...

items.description:
Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ruled on Tuesday to place former President Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds, reversing months of denied requests from the right-wing leader's legal team, according to Reuters.[1]

Bolsonaro, 71, has been serving a 27-year prison sentence since November for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. The house arrest will last for an initial 90-day period, after which Moraes said conditions will be reassessed. "The presence of the requirements necessary for maintaining humanitarian house arrest will be reassessed, including a medical examination if needed," the justice wrote in the decision.[1]

items.title: Oil drops as US sends Iran 15-point ceasefire proposal

featured_image.name: Oil prices drop as U.S. crude inventories show an increase - CNBC

items.description: Oil prices swung sharply on Monday and Tuesday as reports emerged that the United States had sent Iran a 15-point proposal to end the war now in its fourth week, offering a potential off-ramp from a conflict that has roiled global energy markets and sent American gas prices soaring.

items.title: Israeli airstrike hits Christian town north of Beirut for first time

featured_image.name: Airstrike hits Lebanese Christian town north of Beirut ...

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike struck the Christian town of Sahel Alma north of Beirut on Tuesday, marking the first time the area had been targeted in the expanding war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to Lebanese state media and Reuters. There were no immediate reports of casualties, but witnesses told Reuters they heard several blasts and saw white smoke rising from the town.[1][2][3]

The strike represents a widening of Israel's air campaign into areas previously untouched by the conflict, which has killed more than 1,000 people in Lebanon and displaced over one million since fighting escalated on March 2.[4][5]

items.title: Iran charges ships up to $2M for Hormuz passage

featured_image.name: Iran War: Tehran Charges Some Ships Hormuz Transit Fees for Safe Passage -  Bloomberg

items.description:
Iran has begun levying transit fees of up to $2 million per voyage on some commercial vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, effectively creating an informal toll on the world's most critical maritime energy chokepoint, according to Bloomberg.[1]

The payments are being sought on an ad hoc basis and do not appear to be systematic, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Some ships have already made the payment, though the mechanism and currency used remain unclear. Iranian authorities have officially denied that a formal policy exists, calling the reports "unfounded".[2][1]

items.title: US airstrikes kill 15 Iraq PMF fighters, including Anbar commander

featured_image.name: Airstrikes in Iraq on Iran-backed paramilitary alliance kill ...

items.description:
Airstrikes attributed to the United States and Israel killed at least 15 fighters from Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces and wounded 30 others in western Iraq early Tuesday, in the deadliest single attack on the Iran-backed militia coalition since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.

The strikes hit a PMF command headquarters in Iraq's Anbar province during a security meeting attended by senior commanders, according to Reuters. Among the dead was Saad al-Baiji, the PMF's operations commander for Anbar province. The PMF confirmed his death along with 14 of his companions in a statement posted on social media, calling the attack "a treacherous American targeting that struck the operations headquarters".[1][2]

items.title: Netanyahu taps top aide Dermer to vet US-Iran deal

featured_image.name: Netanyahu Taps Ron Dermer to Oversee US-Iran Deal Talks for Israeli  Interests - Bloomberg

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu assigned his closest confidant, former Strategic Affairs Minister Ron Dermer, to monitor US-Iranian negotiations and ensure Israel's core interests are not sacrificed in any potential deal to end the war, according to Bloomberg, citing an Israeli official speaking on condition of anonymity.[1][2]

Dermer's primary focus is on ensuring the dismantlement of Iran's nuclear program and the removal and elimination of roughly 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium — material that Iran reportedly boasted to White House Special Envoy Steve Witkoff was sufficient for 11 nuclear bombs, according to Jewish Insider.[3]

items.title: Trump claims Iran gave US an energy 'present' tied to Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump: 'Major points of agreement' with Iran after talks

items.description:
President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Iran had made a major energy-related concession to the United States, describing it as a gift that "arrived today" — though he offered no specifics and Iran has repeatedly denied engaging in any negotiations with Washington.

"They gave us a present and the present arrived today, and it was a very big present, worth a tremendous amount of money," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, according to Reuters. "It wasn't nuclear; it was oil-and-gas-related, and it was a very nice thing they did."[1]

Trump said the gesture was connected to the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply passes. He characterized it as proof that "we're dealing with the right people" in Tehran and claimed Iran had also agreed it "will never have a nuclear weapon," The Independent reported.[2][3]

items.title: Iran refuses talks with Witkoff and Kushner, eyes Vance

featured_image.name: JD Vance is walking a tightrope on Iran. What does he really think?

items.description:
Iran has refused to continue diplomatic engagement with President Donald Trump's top envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, accusing them of deception in the lead-up to the U.S.-Israeli strikes that began on February 28, according to The Telegraph. Gulf sources told the publication that Tehran now views Vice President JD Vance as its preferred American interlocutor, owing to his well-documented skepticism of military intervention abroad.[1][2]

The shift comes as mediating nations work to arrange a potential meeting in Islamabad, Pakistan, that could bring together Vance and Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf as early as this week.[3][4]

items.title: Denmark's left bloc wins election but falls short of majority

featured_image.name: Exit polls: Frederiksen's Social Democrats win Danish election but probably  no majority

items.description:
Denmark's left-wing bloc led by Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen emerged ahead in Tuesday's parliamentary election but failed to secure a governing majority, with the Social Democrats posting their weakest result in 125 years and leaving centrist Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen positioned as kingmaker in what promises to be weeks of coalition negotiations.

With nearly all votes counted late Tuesday, the "red bloc" of left-leaning parties captured 84 seats in Denmark's 179-seat Folketing, while the right-wing "blue bloc" secured 77 seats — both well short of the 90 needed for a majority. Rasmussen's centrist Moderates, which won 14 seats, now hold the balance of power.[1][2]

items.title: Death toll rises to 69 in Colombia military plane crash

featured_image.name: Colombian military plane crash kills at least 66, wounds dozens

items.description: A Colombian Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane crashed into dense jungle shortly after takeoff on Monday, killing 69 members of the country's security forces in one of the deadliest air disasters in Colombian military history. The death toll, updated Tuesday by the armed forces, also left 57 people injured and one still missing.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iranian missile intercepted over Lebanon in first since regional war began

featured_image.name: Lebanon orders Iran's ambassador out, escalating a postwar ...

items.description: An Iranian ballistic missile was intercepted over Lebanese airspace on Tuesday in what security officials described as the first such incident since the regional war began, sending debris raining down on communities north of Beirut and deepening fears that Lebanon is being drawn further into the expanding conflict between Iran and Israel.

items.title: Iran says drones struck Israeli defense sites, Ben Gurion Airport

featured_image.name: Yemen's Houthis claim targeting Israel's Ben Gurion airport

items.description: Iran's armed forces said on Tuesday that they carried out a series of drone strikes targeting Israeli defense industry facilities and military infrastructure at Ben Gurion Airport, marking the latest escalation in a conflict now in its fourth week.

items.title: Debris from intercepted missiles knocks out 7 Kuwait power lines

featured_image.name: Kuwait Defense Forces: 9 Ballistic Missiles Intercepted Over 24 Hours

items.description:
Kuwait's electricity grid suffered fresh damage on Tuesday after falling debris from intercepted Iranian missiles and drones knocked seven overhead power transmission lines out of service, triggering partial blackouts across several parts of the country.

The Ministry of Electricity, Water, and Renewable Energy confirmed the disruptions late Monday, with spokesperson Eng. Fatima Jawhar Hayat saying the damage resulted from air defense interception activities, according to a statement carried by Kuwait's state news agency KUNA. Technical teams were mobilized but could not begin full assessments until security authorities cleared the affected sites.[1][2][3]

items.title: British troops down 14 drones in record night at Iraq base

featured_image.name: British troops shoot down 14 Iranian 'kamikaze' drones fired ...

items.description: British forces stationed in northern Iraq shot down 14 Iranian "kamikaze" drones overnight on Monday, the Ministry of Defence confirmed on Tuesday, marking the highest number of unmanned aerial vehicles destroyed in a single night since the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran began nearly four weeks ago.[1][2]

items.title: Drone strike hits Kuwait airport fuel tank, no casualties reported

featured_image.name: Drone Strike Damages Kuwait International Airport Terminal 1

items.description: A drone attack struck a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport on Tuesday, igniting a fire but causing no casualties, according to Kuwait's civil aviation authority. The strike is the latest in a series of Iranian retaliatory attacks on Gulf state infrastructure that have repeatedly targeted the airport since late February.[1][2]

items.title: Kuwait destroys 13 missiles, 10 drones as Iran strikes Gulf states

featured_image.name: Kuwait repels drone and missile attacks without casualties

items.description: Kuwait's air defense systems intercepted a barrage of Iranian ballistic missiles and drones early Tuesday, with falling debris damaging homes and knocking out power lines across parts of the country, the Defense Ministry said. No casualties were reported.

items.title: China presses Iran to start peace talks as Gulf war escalates

featured_image.name: China reaffirms support for Iran as top diplomats hold phone ...

items.description:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday, pressing Tehran to seize "every opportunity and window for peace" and begin negotiations to end the war that has engulfed the Middle East since late February. "Talking is always better than to keep fighting," Wang told Araghchi, according to a Chinese foreign ministry statement, adding that "all hotspot issues should be resolved through dialogue and negotiation, not by using force."[1][2][3]

The call, held at Iran's request according to Beijing, comes at a delicate moment. President Donald Trump claimed Monday that the United States had held "very good and productive conversations" with a "top person" in Iran's leadership, and extended by five days a deadline to strike the country's power plants to allow for talks. Tehran has flatly denied any direct negotiations are taking place, with parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accusing Trump of seeking "to manipulate the financial and oil markets."[4][3]
